name: Patscherkofel
kurzbeschreibung: Patscherkofel rises proudly south of Innsbruck, combining Olympic winter sports history with the famed Stone Pine Trail (Zirbenweg) and sweeping valley vistas.
preis: Free access to trails (Patscherkofelbahn cable car charges fares)
oeffnungszeiten: Accessible year-round; cable car operates daily 8:30–17:00 (brief maintenance spring/autumn)
beschreibung:
Überblick

Patscherkofel, with its unmistakable rounded silhouette and high-altitude radio mast standing at 2,246 metres, reigns as Innsbruck's iconic southern mountain sentinel. Renowned worldwide as the venue of the 1964 and 1976 Olympic Downhill races—forever immortalized by Franz Klammer's legendary gold medal run—this mountain holds a treasured place in international sports history. Geologically part of the Tux Alps, Patscherkofel commands sweeping 360-degree panoramas: looking north, the vibrant Inn Valley and the vertical crags of the Nordkette stretch across the horizon, while southwards lies a sea of glaciated summits in the Stubai and Zillertal Alps. Ancient, aromatic stone pine forests drape its shoulders, creating an exquisite alpine sanctuary renowned for clean mountain air and ecological serenity.

Route & Anforderungen

The network of trails weaving across Patscherkofel caters to everyone from casual sightseers to active hikers. The ultra-modern 10-seater Patscherkofel gondola sweeps passengers effortlessly from the valley base near Igls up to the mountain station at 1,965 metres. From there, a well-graded gravel path leads uphill in about one hour to the summit cross and the historic Patscherkofel Alpine Shelter. The undisputed highlight is the legendary Stone Pine Trail (Zirbenweg), an undulating panoramic path traversing roughly seven kilometers through one of Europe's oldest and largest contiguous Swiss stone pine forests to the Tulfeinalm. Standard trainers suffice for broad paths around the station, whereas sturdy ankle-high hiking boots and windproof layers are advised for the summit ascent.

Besuch & Anreise

Travel from Innsbruck is swift, taking just ten to fifteen minutes by car via Igls or Patsch along the historic Römerstraße to the valley station. The public transit connection is exceptionally convenient via Innsbruck city bus Line J, which runs directly from the city centre to the lift terminal every ten minutes. Ample parking is provided at the base terminal with ticket validation discounts for cable car guests.

Tipps

Take advantage of the Zirbenweg Circular Ticket, which includes rides on both the Patscherkofel and Glungezer lifts as well as the connecting regional shuttle bus. Near the top gondola station, visit the Alpengarten Patscherkofel, Austria's highest botanical garden operated by the University of Innsbruck.
